name: Eastern Qiandong Miao
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: zh.wikipedia, 苗语黔东方言 (wikitext, fetched sources 2026-09-17).
sources.note: Tertiary. 东部土语 '以锦屏县偶里乡的语音为代表音'; '黔东方言各土语都有八个声调，没有连读变调现象'; no 重音/轻声 statement.

sources.citation: Schiering, René & Harry van der Hulst. 2010. Word accent systems in the languages of Asia. In van der Hulst, Goedemans & van Zanten (eds.), A survey of word accentual patterns in the languages of the world, 509-599. Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: publisher record (DOI); no open copy and no Harvard e-access found (also: publisher (doi, likely paywalled))
sources.note: Second-hand, family-level: p.596 lists 'Eastern Qiandong Hmong'; 'Hmong-Mien is usually described as being exclusively tonal, but that does not imply that the languages in this family couldn't be accentual as well... we did not have access to sources that would allow us to elaborate on this point.' No language-specific data.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page east2370 'Eastern Qiandong Miao' (subgroup Eastern Qiandongic Miao = east2370 + sanq1234 Sanqiao).
sources.note: Bibliography only; sole descriptive ref = 湖南省民族志修订稿 III (1960).

sources.citation: en.wikipedia, 'Sanqiao language' (wikitext, fetched sources 2026-09-17); cites Hsiu 2024 SEALS 33 and Yu Dazhong 2017.
sources.note: Nothing; sister lect sanq1234 in Jinping/Liping.

sources.citation: Brunelle, Marc, James Kirby, Alexis Michaud & Justin Watkins. 2020. Prosodic systems: Mainland Southeast Asia (preprint).
sources.note: Areal survey; Hmong-Mien tone/phonation only (Black Miao example); nothing on Hmu word stress.

sources.citation: Ratliff, Martha. 2010. Hmong-Mien language history (Pacific Linguistics 613). Canberra.
sources.note: East Hmongic represented only by Yanghao (northern vernacular); nothing on the eastern vernacular or its stress.

sources.citation: en.wikipedia, 'Hmu language' (wikitext, fetched sources 2026-09-17), incl. Eastern vernacular sub-lects after Tu Guanglu & Yang Jun 2008 锦屏县汉侗苗语方言志 and an 8-tone table for Ouli 偶里 (Jinping).
sources.note: Tertiary. 'All dialects have eight tones. There is no sandhi'; Eastern (偶里) tone values 33 42 22 21 45 55 24 12, tones 3 and 8 breathy. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Wang Fushi 王辅世 (主编). 1985. 苗语简志 Miaoyu jianzhi. Beijing: 民族出版社.
sources.note: Silent for hmq. p.104 only locates the 黔东方言东部土语 (c. 200,000 speakers; 锦屏、黎平、剑河; 湖南靖县、通道、会同); p.5 Miao-wide: every native syllable = initial + rhyme + tone; no eastern-vernacular data; the only 轻声 remark (p.12) concerns Layiping (Xiangxi) prefixes.

sources.citation: Miao Language Team, Chinese Academy of Sciences 1962 [trans. 1972]. A brief description of the Miao language. In H. C. Purnell (ed.), Miao and Yao linguistic studies (Cornell SEAP Data Paper 88), pp. 1-25.
sources.note: Miao-wide only (Ch'ien-tung dialect said to cover Chin p'ing, Li p'ing, T'ung tao): p.5 'Every syllable has a specific tone which serves to distinguish lexical meaning' and 'With the exception of the Ch'ien tung dialect... all types of Miao have tone sandhi'. No statement on word stress; data point for Qiandong is Yanghao (northern vernacular).

sources.citation: Ma Hsueh-liang 马学良 & T'ai Ch'ang-hou 邰昌厚. 1956 [trans. 1972]. A preliminary comparison of the phonology of the Miao dialects in southeastern Kweichow [贵州省东南部苗语语音的初步比较, 语言研究 1: 265-282]. In H. C. Purnell (ed.), Miao and Yao linguistic studies (Cornell SEAP Data Paper 88), pp. 27ff. Ithaca.
sources.note: Silent. 21 survey points incl. Chin p'ing 锦屏 and Ching hsien 靖县 (Hunan), both in the eastern-vernacular area; treats initials, finals and tone categories only. p.50: 'Ching hsien also has seven tones, the fourth and eighth tone categories having merged with the value 22' and 'Chin p'ing has seven tones, the fourth and eighth tone categories having merged with the value 13'. The word 'stress' never occurs.

sources.citation: Tu Guanglu 涂光禄 & Yang Jun 杨军. 2008. 锦屏县汉侗苗语方言志 [Gazetteer of the Chinese, Dong and Miao dialects of Jinping County]. Guiyang: 贵州大学出版社. ISBN 978-7-81126-044-1.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Only known book-length description of Jinping Miao (Ouli 偶里 = representative point of the eastern vernacular, plus Hekou and Yuhe sub-lects); its 苗语音系 chapter is the most likely place for a 轻声/重音 or syllable-prominence remark specific to hmq.
